# How to create a Content Brief with Content Brief Generator that will help your SEO efforts

![Tom Winter](https://secure.gravatar.com/avatar/aa3b486402b5373030fb440224625e145ee725201cf4b9238dcb40be1e167f88?s=40&d=mm&r=g)[Tom Winter](https://seowind.io/author/seowind/ "Posts by Tom Winter")August 9, 2024

If you’re like most marketers, you know that high-quality content is essential for a successful SEO strategy. But what about the actual process of creating that content? It can be tough to know where to start, especially if you’re not sure what your audience is looking for. A content brief can help with that. In this blog post, we’ll show you how to create a [content brief that will help your SEO efforts, and we’ll also provide a handy content brief generator](https://seowind.io/seo-content-brief-generator/) to make things easier. Let’s get started!

## Why Should You Use a Content Brief?

In a layperson’s language, we can understand a [content brief](https://seowind.io/content-brief/) as a document, which defines the tone, and fundamental structure and elucidates other requirements of a piece of content before it is sent to the writer. Hence, a tool that helps individuals and agencies define content expectations is a content brief generator. There are several veritable advantages of using a content brief, the first being quality improvement and saving precious time during the content creation process. In simple words, a good content brief makes the content execution process smoother and more efficient.

### No Guesswork

Needless to say, a content brief offers a lucid idea to the writers on what they should include in a write-up, leaving no room for guesswork and confusion.

### Lesser Rewrites and Revisions

Content briefs enable the entire content team, from strategists to writers and editors to align the tasks, thereby preventing miscommunication. The better the communication, the lesser the chances of revisions and rewrites.

### Timely Delivery

Without clear guidelines, back-and-forth revisions are unavoidable. As such, a content brief erases the tediousness of multiple rewrites and helps the content team with timely delivery.

### No Missing Out on Critical Content

Another crucial benefit of opting for a content brief is that it serves as a [checklist for the writer](https://seowind.io/blog-post-checklist/), editor, and so forth. By highlighting the subtopics, facts, and questions you want in your content, you can assist the writing team in seamlessly producing comprehensive writeups that search engines adore.

Now that we have touched upon the basics of the topic, if you want to know how to write a content brief, read ahead.

## Six Important Aspects of Content Brief

There are specific foolproof rules to writing a top-notch content brief that will elevate your website goals in an unprecedented fashion. The key is to include the following aspects in your content brief.

### 1\. Target Audience

Mentioning the [target audience](https://neilpatel.com/blog/target-audience/) is an easy yet proven method to improve the efficiency of any content piece. As such, it is essential to mention the content audience in your content brief. Your target audience is the cohort your business aims to reach via the concerned content, and the audience has distinctive characteristics vis-a-vis age, geographic location, interests, professions, etc. Elaborating on the said factors and explaining to the writer the niche of the content is the first aspect of an excellent content brief. If you find it challenging to explain the nitty-gritty of your target audience, a content brief generator might help.

### 2\. The tone of the Voice and Company Description

The second indispensable aspect of a content brief is the company description. You should provide the writer with a crisp overview of what your brand or company is about so they can understand and align the structure and mandates of the write-up they will prepare. The pointer is especially important if you are working with a writer for the first time. Likewise, you should acquaint the content team with your company’s overall tone so they can deliver the best results. The purpose of including ‘tone’ in a content brief is to help writers gauge the nuances of your brand so that they can prepare a write-up that fits into your brand and your business ethos.

### 3\. High-quality Content Outline

A good-quality [content outline](https://seowind.io/content-outline-article-blog/) can help writers take the content to a notch higher, ultimately facilitating your business goals. A content outline defines the structure of the write-up that your site requires and includes a list of the headings and sub-headings. The outline does have to be exhaustive or brutally rigid, but it is a feasible idea to mention what you consider an absolute necessity. At times, tools like a brief generator might also come in handy. It is noteworthy to mention that if you have something concrete in your mind, come with the title and Meta description yourself instead of outsourcing the same to the writer. In a nutshell, an outline in the content brief minimizes the rewrites and revisions for the content writer and ensures that you get timely delivery and uncompromised quality.

### 4\. Keyword Suggestions

Long gone are the days when the repetition of the targetted keyword was all that was required to beat the Google algorithm. Nowadays, with the constant SEO alterations like the Panda Update, Helpful Content Update, etc., of Google, it is imperative to include suggested keywords in the content brief. Defining the subject of the blog or article coupled with the keywords are foundational aspects of a sound content brief.

### 5\. Examples of the Content You Like

A good content brief does not end with a crisp outline or keyword suggestions; it should also include examples of resources that you like and would want the writer to emulate and take inspiration from. Opting for examples in a good brief helps writers and the entire content team grasp your expectations in HD and incorporate the same in the write-up. Consequently, you can also include resources you despise to give the writers a clue on what they should avoid.

### 6\. The Required Content-Length

The last and most essential component of a [good content brief is the desired length](https://www.searchenginejournal.com/ranking-factors/content-length/) of the content. To begin with, lengthier writeups do not imply better quality or a higher SERP rank. Google wants your article to be relevant, organic, and cater to the needs of the [user search intent](https://seowind.io/user-search-intent-seo/). As such, the length of the content should be amenable to the aforesaid factors. If your clientele is looking for short content, a 2000-word article will be a major turn-off. Contrarily, if your target audience is aligned to long-form blogs, a crisp overview of the topic in 500 words will not suffice. Balance and awareness are the keys to determining the content length, and you should communicate the same to your writer via the content brief. If gauging out the length of the content seems too intimidating, then a tool like a content brief generator ought to help.

Now that we know how to write a content brief let’s understand how it can influence your site’s SEO.

## FAQs about SEO Content Briefs

### **Q.1. What does an SEO content brief mean?**

To ensure that all parties engaged in creating content are on the same page about its goal and the types of items that should be included, an SEO brief, also known as an SEO content brief, is often used.

### **Q.2. Why are SEO content briefs important?**

Writers and clients can use the guidelines and structure provided in a content brief to consistently generate SEO-competitive outcomes without spending the time or mental capacity otherwise required to hone in on optimization. Instead of worrying about optimization, you can focus on integrating the skills and value additions provided by SEO.

### **Q.3. What are the characteristics of an SEO-centric content brief?**

There are numerous varieties of content briefs, one of which is an SEO-centric one. It’s one of a kind because it’s meant to serve as guidance for the writer as they craft content to attract visitors via organic search results.

### **Q.4. What should an SEO content brief contain?**

The following things are a must include in the SEO content brief:

- Key focus and motivation for the search. Including a query, and the target is essential for any SEO-focused content brief.
- Format.
- Matters of discussion and questions to be addressed.
- The phase of the funnel.
- The desired outcome you hope your readers will take after reading your work.
- Possibilities to link internally and externally.
